title: The Cluny Mews Silence
scene: Rain swept Cluny Mews at 11:40 p.m. when Edwin Vale was found beneath the brass stairwell lamp, a single blow to the temple delivered with the building’s missing iron letter opener. The lock had not been forced; the killer was expected.

Gemma.alibi: Said she was sorting keys in the foyer; the porter saw the glint of her round glasses on the upper landing.
Gemma.relationship: Vale had threatened to expose her forged tenancy papers.

Brendan Alper.alibi: Signed for tea at the Canterbury Club before the rain began.
Brendan Alper.relationship: A former schoolmate who owed Vale a modest loan.

Kyle Tucker.alibi: His wide-brim hat was dripping at Pier Nine, where two dockhands saw him unload crates.
Kyle Tucker.relationship: Vale had brokered one of his freight contracts.

James Kirimi.alibi: Logged a delayed coach departure from the transport control room.
James Kirimi.relationship: A client whose routes Vale managed.

Stanley.alibi: Was still seated at the dinner gathering across town.
Stanley.relationship: A neighbor who disliked Vale’s parties.

Mama.alibi: Held court at a syndicate supper until midnight.
Mama.relationship: Vale once rented her a warehouse.

Marley.alibi: Was seen on a nearby roof after the bell rang.
Marley.relationship: Had been caught trespassing in Vale’s flats.

Dilly.alibi: Waited in the service alley with the delivery boys.
Dilly.relationship: Marley’s lookout and no friend of Vale.

confession: Gemma finally admits she used the letter opener when Vale reached for the tenancy ledger. “He knew the papers were false,” she says, “and he meant to make a spectacle of it.”

title: Last Stop at Ashdown
scene: At 10:15 p.m., after the final matinee emptied, Rosa Bell lay behind the velvet curtain of the Ashdown Picture House. A projector-reel weight had struck her skull; dust on the floor showed one set of polished shoe prints leading toward the timetable office.

Gemma.alibi: Bought a ticket at the front desk; her round glasses were noted by the cashier.
Gemma.relationship: Bell had once let her into a sold-out show.

Brendan Alper.alibi: Was seen crossing the Canterbury arcade with his moustache tucked behind a scarf.
Brendan Alper.relationship: Bell rejected his invitation to the premiere.

Kyle Tucker.alibi: The harbour watchman recognized his wide-brim hat at the freighter gate.
Kyle Tucker.relationship: Bell had no known business with him.

James Kirimi.alibi: Claimed he was checking bus schedules, but no service ran from the timetable office that night.
James Kirimi.relationship: Bell had discovered his forged transport vouchers.

Stanley.alibi: A waiter placed him at the dinner gathering through dessert.
Stanley.relationship: Bell was his cousin’s former roommate.

Mama.alibi: Received three callers at her supper table during the time of death.
Mama.relationship: Bell sold her old cinema posters.

Marley.alibi: A projectionist saw the pointed-eared figure near the roof vent before the show.
Marley.relationship: Bell had fed Marley scraps after closing.

Dilly.alibi: The ushering staff saw Dilly by the alley exit when the curtain fell.

confession: James Kirimi breaks beneath the projector’s glare. “Rosa had the vouchers,” he confesses. “She was going to hand them to the inspector before the credits rolled.”

title: The Pearl Pin Affair
scene: At 1:05 a.m. in the locked counting room of Crowe & Sons, Felix Crowe was found facedown beside an open safe. A pearl pin rested under his hand, while the only window stood latched from inside and the watchman heard a familiar voice leave by the front door.

Gemma.alibi: The night tram conductor recalled her round glasses in the rear carriage.
Gemma.relationship: Crowe had appraised a brooch for her.

Brendan Alper.alibi: His academy friends saw him leave the Canterbury Club together.
Brendan Alper.relationship: Crowe had refused to value his family ring.

Kyle Tucker.alibi: Was unloading a Bermuda crate beneath the wide brim of his hat.
Kyle Tucker.relationship: Crowe authenticated cargo jewellery for him.

James Kirimi.alibi: A dispatcher called him from the transport office at one o’clock.
James Kirimi.relationship: Crowe supplied a collector on his route.

Stanley.alibi: The dinner host heard him make a toast at midnight and remain for coffee.
Stanley.relationship: Crowe had been invited to his gathering.

Mama.alibi: Said she never left supper, yet the pearl pin at the scene matches the one fixed to her cloche hat.
Mama.relationship: Crowe was about to testify about her uncut gems.

Marley.alibi: A rooftop gardener saw Marley chasing a pigeon after midnight.
Marley.relationship: Crowe kept Marley out of his shop windows.

Dilly.alibi: The service porter gave Dilly directions to the alley at 12:50.
Dilly.relationship: Dilly had never met Crowe directly.

confession: Mama smooths her cloche hat and leaves the pearl pin on the desk. “Crowe was selling my secrets,” she says. “The safe opened for me because it always did.”
